With Spack and E4S recipes, each specialized layer compiled 1 of 20 buildable packages at two facilities, Midway3 and NSF ACCESS Anvil. On Anvil, each further GPU target adds 1,412 files where a monolithic build adds 10,772, rebuilding a layer is 1.8 to 2.8 times faster, and application performance is unchanged on A100 and H100 GPUs. The same install trees run unmodified under Apptainer and Charliecloud. The poster also reports four constraints on where reuse holds.

events.title: Useful Data, Not Just More Data: Cost-Aware Floating Car Data Generation in Large-Scale Traffic Simulation
events.description: Large-scale traffic simulations can generate millions of floating car data (FCD) records, but more output does not necessarily provide more useful information. Using Ruth on LUMI, we study a Chicago scenario with 6.9 million input vehicle trips and 748,509 road-network nodes. We compare output size, road-edge coverage, temporal coverage, and speed similarity against a high-detail simulation reference. With vehicle updates fixed at 20 seconds, increasing the FCD sampling period from 5 to 20 seconds halves output while retaining 97.1% road-edge coverage and 88.9% temporal coverage. Tests on 1–16 nodes show sublinear gains in the traffic-time interval recorded within a fixed wall-time budget. Reducing rerouting participation from 80% to 50% extends this interval by 18%–22% and lowers wall time per second of recorded traffic time by 15%–18%. We recommend selecting the smallest output meeting task-specific coverage and speed-error requirements; rerouting changes still require validation of traffic outcomes.

events.title: VLIW Scheduling: Timing Is All You Need
events.description:
AMD's XDNA2 NPU packs 32 six-issue VLIW cores where the schedule must resolve nearly all pipeline hazards. Each core achieves 1,843 GFLOPS by always issuing a VMAC.F operation, an 8×8×8 block-floating-point (BFP16) matrix multiply-accumulate. This corresponds to an array-wide performance of 59 TFLOPS. One obstacle is register pressure: a standard double-buffered 2×2 output block needs eight accumulator registers, whereas a core has only five.

We present a hand-scheduled VLIW BFP16 tensor-contraction kernel that time-multiplexes the output block's four accumulation chains onto two registers and issues a VMAC.F in every steady-state cycle.

On one core with L1-resident data, our kernel achieves 96.4% of theoretical peak (5.0× faster than the compiled mm_bfp.cc kernel). With the operands streamed from DRAM, a pre-tiled M3840×N3840×K8192 matrix multiplication reaches 21.4 TFLOPS on the whole NPU.

At the poster, we will walk visitors through the VLIW scheduling diagrams and the scannable artifact reproducing every measurement.

events.title: VisKnacks: Agentic ParaView Visualization on HPC
events.description: Artificial intelligence can assist in prototyping scientific visualizations. To assist visualization experts, we introduce VisKnacks, an autonomous ParaView visualization agent enabled by large language models (LLMs). VisKnacks integrates multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and containerized rendering services for high performance computing (HPC) systems while remaining compatible with existing agent harnesses. The system supports hybrid workflows in which ParaView rendering is distributed to HPC resources while pipeline creation and iterative refinement remain local. We present the system overview, initial benchmarks, visualization quality benchmarks, and lessons learned from deploying this system.

events.title: VisionHPC: AI Generation of Expert-Level HPC Codes From High-Level Mathematical Abstractions
events.description: We present VisionHPC, an agentic AI framework that generates expert-level high performance computing (HPC) code directly from high-level mathematical abstractions. Following extensive expert-guided training, it produces HPC implementations for multicore CPUs and GPUs using widely adopted parallel programming models, including OpenMP, OpenACC, and CUDA/HIP. The framework accepts images of mathematical formulations from three representative scientific domains — linear algebra, partial differential equations, and computational fluid dynamics — and translates them into efficient parallel code. Compared with state-of-the-art multimodal models, including ChatGPT, MathGPT, and Claude, VisionHPC achieves up to 12× higher correctness than the strongest baseline, reaching an average correctness exceeding 95%. These results demonstrate that AI can reliably bridge high-level mathematical descriptions and expert-quality HPC software, substantially improving productivity for scientific software development.

events.title: When More Cores Hurts: The Vector Database Scaling Paradox in HPC
events.description: Vector databases have been designed and optimized for cloud environments; however, emerging scientific AI workloads (e.g., molecular search, meteorological trajectory detection, and literature-driven hypothesis generation) demand efficient, scalable execution on HPC systems. We present a large-scale evaluation of three state-of-the-art vector databases — Qdrant, Milvus, and Weaviate — on two production supercomputers, scaling to 256 distributed workers across 64 compute nodes. We evaluate VDBs using Yandex-T2I, a multimodal embedding dataset, and Pes2o-VE, a novel real-world scientific dataset. Our results reveal that insertion is bottlenecked by per-batch consistency requirements, additional cores can reduce query throughput by up to 30.67%, and scaling from 16 to 256 workers yields a 2.67x improvement with 16 nodes before QPS begins to decline. This scaling paradox exposes the fundamental mismatch between cloud-oriented designs and HPC systems, highlighting the need for new, HPC-aware vector database designs.

A Parallel Algorithm for the Construction of Partial Information Decomposition-Based Genome-Scale Networks from Single-Cell Datasets
events.description: Methods for constructing gene networks from tissue-level expression data, developed over the past two decades, are being reassessed for applicability to single-cell datasets. The higher noise and sparsity of single-cell data demand more robust, computationally intensive approaches, while also requiring scalability to orders-of-magnitude larger datasets. We focus on PIDC, an information-theoretic method that produces high-quality networks from single-cell data but incurs $O(n^3)$ runtime for $n$ genes, limiting scalability even with parallelization. We present a novel sequential algorithm that reduces complexity to $O(n^2 \log n)$, along with its distributed-memory parallelization achieving $O(n^2/p + T_{sort}(n^2, p))$ time, where $p$ is the number of processors and $T_{sort}$ is the time for parallel sorting. On 64 cores, our MPI implementation achieves a 158X speedup over the existing PIDC algorithm. We further demonstrate construction of a genome-scale human gene network with 30,000 genes from 800,000 cells in 2.5 hours using 2,048 cores.

events.title: Scalable Search and Data Analytics for Scientific Discovery
events.description: The papers make search and analysis over massive scientific data tractable: genome-scale gene-network construction, aggressively pruned cancer mutation-combination search, visualization-aware particle-data representation, and RT-core accelerated exact high-dimensional similarity search.

events.title: Mercury: Practical User-Space API Remoting for Secure Containers in Public Clouds
events.description:
In public cloud environments, secure containers face challenges in device virtualization due to their micro virtual machine architecture. We introduce Mercury, a user-space API remoting framework co-designed with our secure container RunD. Mercury leverages a dynamic shared memory interface between guest and host, along with KVM hypercalls for efficient notifications.

When applied to CUDA, Mercury preserves API semantics across virtualization boundaries, enabling GPU virtualization with under 4% overhead during large language model inference. Mercury also achieves a 20% speedup compared to existing API remoting solutions. Building on Mercury, we deploy GPU sharing and checkpoint/restore in Alibaba Cloud, effectively doubling GPU deployment density and reducing cold start latency by over 95% in practice.

events.title: Secure, Sustainable, and Elastic Cloud HPC
events.description: The papers address secure and elastic cloud-style HPC services while considering storage lifetime and environmental impact. The panel discussion can center on which cloud abstractions are appropriate for future HPC.

events.title: Best Papers: Accelerator-Centric Scientific Performance
events.description: These papers push accelerator performance through GPU compression, tensor-core evaluation, shared-memory optimization, and ultra-low-latency collectives. The session showcases advances across the scientific computing stack.

events.title: FSZ: Breaking the Prediction-Throughput Trade-Off in GPU Lossy Compression
events.description: Existing fast GPU error-bounded lossy compressors achieve high throughput with pure-GPU single-kernel designs, but their compression ratios remain limited because they apply a fixed first-order predictor on independent blocks. We propose FSZ, a GPU error-bounded lossy compressor that redesigns the prediction stage with three innovations within a single CUDA kernel: (1) cross-block prediction state carries Lorenzo state across block boundaries within 256-element tiles, eliminating seven of eight boundary residuals; (2) per-tile adaptive multi-order prediction and centering selects the best strategy for each tile; and (3) a single-pass four-way evaluation exploits a property of finite differences to evaluate all variants from one data read, within a fixed predictor's bandwidth budget. On NVIDIA GH200 with eight real-world datasets, FSZ outperforms cuSZp-P by up to 10.95x and cuSZp-O by up to 2.92x in compression ratio while achieving the highest average throughput (676 GB/s compression, 785 GB/s decompression) among all evaluated compressors.

events.title: Resource-Aware LLM Serving Pipelines
events.description: The papers address multi-stage and KV-constrained LLM serving through memory allocation, micro-task parallelism, pipeline design, and preemptive scheduling. Together they present a coherent resource-management view of inference.

events.title: When KV Meets Embeddings: Dynamic GPU Memory Allocation for Accelerating Generative Recommender Serving
events.description:
Generative recommender (GR) inference faces a dual memory bottleneck absent in LLM serving. Embedding hot caches and KV caches compete for limited GPU HBM, while existing systems optimize them in isolation, leading to suboptimal tail latency. We observe that (1) the optimal EMB–KV memory allocation ratio shifts by up to 0.35 across workloads, and (2) static allocations leave 20%–30% latency improvement untapped, while continuous reallocation risks cache thrashing and P99 SLO violations.

We present RACER, which jointly and adaptively allocates HBM at runtime. It addresses two challenges: (1) adaptive memory allocation via a three-layer PPO controller with online adaptation and burst recovery, achieving 32 μs decision latency; and (2) embedding-KV-aware scheduling that maximizes joint EMB–KV cache reuse across nodes.

Evaluations on three production-scale datasets show that RACER reduces P99 latency by 24%–38% over the best static strategy and achieves 93.5%–99.6% SLO satisfaction, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines (67%–94.2%) without sacrificing throughput.

events.title: CoreFlow: Context-Centric Resource Management for LLM-Based Agentic Workflows
events.description:
The rise of agentic workflows, which coordinate multiple LLM-based agents to tackle complex tasks, has shifted the LLM serving toward a multi-step, context-driven execution paradigm. This shift introduces highly skewed context-length distributions and agent-specific KV cache-reuse patterns in LLM workloads, challenging existing resource management systems that remain oblivious to these characteristics.

This paper introduces CoreFlow, a context-centric resource management system tailored for the distinct execution patterns of agentic workflows. CoreFlow incorporates three key designs: (1) hierarchical performance modeling, which captures the effects of context-length variance and imbalanced cache reuse inherent in context-driven execution; (2) dual-level resource optimization, combining workflow-level allocation to distribute resources across agents with agent-level partitioning to isolate requests with heterogeneous context lengths; and (3) adaptive cache management, which aligns cache placement with resource partitioning while minimizing cache-swap overhead. Evaluations on representative workflows demonstrate that CoreFlow reduces end-to-end latency by 57.6% and improves workflow throughput by 63.1%.

events.title: Papers in Conversation: AI Inference Becomes an HPC Systems Problem
events.description: Three papers treat LLM inference as a full HPC systems problem: managing agent context, serving experts as distributed services, and coordinating prefill and decode for goodput. The panel can examine whether future AI supercomputers need fundamentally different schedulers and resource abstractions.

events.title: Emerging Storage Technology
events.description:
The AI and HPC community is scrambling to accommodate the explosive demand for memory and storage capacity and new technologies. Does one solution fit all in storage components and architectures? What new differentiators matter across varied usages like out-of-core HPC computation on huge data sets, context memory cache capacity for LLM inference, 10x-higher IOPs for vector databases and GNNs, scaled checkpointing, and multitenant security?

To spark creativity and frame emerging opportunities, this panel gathers leading experts from academia in usage models, and vendor technologists for storage microcontrollers, object/file systems, and network storage acceleration that engage in storage innovation. The audience will gain new knowledge of emerging tech and new perspectives on topics that they may have recently heard of. Just as for each of the last several years of this Panel/BoF, speakers and audience contributors will archive reference material to accelerate moving the broader community forward.

events.title: Emerging Storage Technology
Medical Digital Twins: Can HPC Unite the Future for Health Globally?
events.description: Medical digital twins are an exciting area of investment and rapid innovation and hold tremendous potential to realize the promise of precision medicine and improved health. The successful adoption of medical digital twin approaches requires a community effort, spanning a full range of stakeholders with the individual or patient at the center. With an esteemed group of experts in medical digital twins, the panel will help attendees understand the world of medical digital twins, what it means and what it holds in store. The panel will also discuss several areas where HPC plays or could play a role in helping to unify and connect medical digital twin stakeholders in such areas as varying disciplines, anatomical systems, interoperability, data access and privacy, proprietary and open, AI and mechanistic models, clinics and research, education, and many more areas essential to the development and adoption of medical digital twins.

Inference in Motion: Storage-Tier KV Cache Offload for Agentic AI
events.description:
Agentic AI systems don't make one inference call, they fork many, and each fork recomputes attention over its context unless that computation can be reused. Key-value (KV) caching enables reuse, but agentic fan-out and multi-user concurrency routinely push cache footprints past GPU and host memory, forcing evictions that erase the savings.

We ran a controlled study on an NVIDIA GH200 node, pushing KV working sets past each memory tier in turn. At a representative ~400 GiB multi-user working set, the GPU-only and host-RAM-backed tiers both fell back to full recompute, costing 17-18 seconds to first token. A shared storage tier restored the same context in about 1 second, and adding more GPUs didn't help: the bottleneck is I/O-bound, not compute-bound. This talk walks through that setup, what the I/O trace showed about storage requirements for KV cache offload, and how to test your own infrastructure the same way.

events.title: HPC Cooling and Lifespans
Scaling Liquid Cooling for AI Infrastructure: The Critical Role of Interoperability, Cleanliness, Traceability, and Ecosystem Alignment
events.description: As AI and HPC deployments scale, the next bottleneck is no longer cooling technology itself, but the ability to deploy liquid cooling infrastructure consistently across a complex ecosystem of suppliers, integrators, and operators. Through real-world deployment insights, this session explores how interoperability, cleanliness management, traceability, and standardization influence deployment reliability, operational efficiency, and long-term scalability.

events.title: Before the Qubits Scale: What Quantum Can Learn From the AI Regulation Debate
events.description: As governments debate how to regulate artificial intelligence, a question is emerging in the background: What about quantum? In this moderated discussion, David Awschalom and Robert W. Karr Jr. explore how the regulatory needs of the two fields diverge; from the pace of deployment and the nature of the risks to the role of national security, export controls, and data protection. They'll also ask what quantum can learn from AI's rocky path to regulation, including the costs of acting too late, the risks of over-regulating too early, and the value of building trust and standards alongside the technology. Moderated by John Towns, deputy director of the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA) at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

events.title: Regional Tech Hub: Quantum
events.description:
From understanding the promise of quantum technologies to seeing how they could become part of the communications and computing infrastructure of the future.

Together, the two invited talks will give attendees both a big-picture view of the quantum landscape and a concrete look at how quantum networking is becoming a reality — while exploring how we can structure quantum technologies today for the needs and success of future users.

events.title: StarLight Software Defined Staright Exchange for Data-Intensive Science
Robust Score-Bounded Search for Multi-Hit Carcinogenic Gene Combination Identification
events.description: Cancer arises from combinations of somatic mutations (hits), and identifying these combinations is critical for understanding carcinogenesis and enabling targeted therapies. This task can be formulated as a weighted set cover problem, yet exhaustive enumeration leads to exponential search space growth as the number of hits increases, limiting prior enumeration-based work to at most five-hit combinations even on large-scale supercomputers. We propose a novel algorithm that decomposes higher-order combinations through a shortest addition chain and formulates sample coverage computation as matrix multiplication. It employs a robust score-bounded search strategy that eliminates unpromising candidates without evaluation, while guaranteeing that the best-scoring combination is never discarded. Experiments show our method visits less than one-millionth of prior search spaces, identifies four-hit combinations in about five seconds on a single GPU, outperforms thousand-node supercomputers by orders of magnitude, and extends practical reach of enumeration-based cancer screening from five-hit to nine-hit combinations.

events.title: No Disk Left Behind: Lifetime-Aware Oversubscription of Thin Provisioned Storage in Cloud IaaS Platforms
events.description:
Cloud resource oversubscription is widely used to improve infrastructure utilization, particularly for CPU resources. In contrast, storage resources remain largely statically provisioned despite significant underutilization. Our analysis of multiple OVHcloud platforms shows that virtual machines use on average only 42.9% of their local disk capacity.

In this paper, we explore disk oversubscription in thin-provisioned environments. Unlike CPU, storage resources are persistent and difficult to predict in the black-box context of IaaS platforms. To address these challenges, we introduce Wave, a dynamic oversubscription method that anticipates waves of disk capacity released by virtual machine (VM) churn.

Using large-scale traces from OVHcloud, we show that Wave can reduce required disk capacity by up to 2× while maintaining a low rate of corrective migrations. Beyond infrastructure efficiency, this reduction translates into significant environmental benefits, lowering storage-related Scope 3 emissions by approximately 44.5% in newer cloud regions.

events.title: Do We Need Tensor Cores for Stencil Computations?
events.description: Stencil computation is a fundamental kernel in scientific computing, widely used in applications such as fluid dynamics and weather simulation. Although stencils are traditionally considered memory-bound and thus ill-suited for compute-oriented Tensor Cores, recent studies report substantial acceleration, creating an apparent contradiction. This paper resolves this discrepancy through a systematic performance analysis of stencil computations on Tensor Cores. We revisit stencil-to-Tensor-Core mappings, quantify the computational redundancy introduced by hardware-driven transformations, and develop an enhanced performance model that captures arithmetic-intensity shifts under temporal fusion. From this model, we derive analytical criteria that provide a first-order estimate of whether Tensor Cores will outperform, match, or underperform CUDA Cores for a given stencil and hardware setting. Our analysis identifies the performance sweet spot for Tensor Core acceleration. Evaluations on NVIDIA GPUs with state-of-the-art implementations, including EBISU, ConvStencil, and SPIDER, validate our criteria and show its value for guiding stencil optimization.

events.title: Efficient Serving for Agentic LLM Workflows via Micro-Task-Level Parallelism
events.description: Agentic large language model (LLM) workflows leverage the advanced capabilities of LLMs to instantiate a multi-agent paradigm, where each LLM invocation constitutes an agentic task. Existing optimizations rely on coarse-grained task-level scheduling, which fails to exploit fine-grained parallelism within the workflow, leading to resource underutilization and bursty latency. In this paper, we present Grape, a full-stack LLM system for serving agentic LLM workflows that fully exploits micro-task (μTask)-level parallelism. On the frontend, Grape proposes the TaskFlow abstraction to provide a declarative interface for workflow orchestration. Subsequently, Grape decomposes tasks represented in TaskFlow into fine-grained μTasks that expose the parallelism within the workflow. For the LLM engine, Grape adopts a μTasks-aware scheduling policy with SLO-derived constraints to ensure low-latency execution with improved resource utilization. Moreover, Grape also proposes a dedicated memory management mechanism to alleviate KV Cache memory pressure. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of Grape over state-of-the-art solutions.

events.title: Expert-as-a-Service: Towards Efficient, Scalable, and Robust Large-Scale MoE Serving
events.description: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models challenge serving infrastructures with dynamic, sparse expert utilization, causing instability on conventional systems designed for dense architectures. We propose EaaS, a novel serving system to enable efficient, scalable, and robust MoE deployment. Our system disaggregates MoE modules into independent, stateless services. This design enables fine-grained resource scaling and provides inherent fault tolerance by decoupling compute units. The architecture is powered by a high-performance, CPU-free peer-to-peer communication library that ensures minimal overhead and high throughput. Experiments confirm EaaS's scalability and efficiency, achieving performance comparable to monolithic systems while providing robust fault tolerance and strong scalability. EaaS incurs less than a 2% throughput reduction under simulated hardware failures that would otherwise halt monolithic architectures. It further saves up to 37.5% of computing resources through dynamic fine-grained adaptation to serving traffic, demonstrating strong resilience for large-scale MoE deployment in production.

events.title: Comfort Dogs
Elevating Hybrid Storage From a Capacity to Capability Layer RDMA for S3-Compatible Storage: Removing the Access-Path Barrier to Hot-Path Object I/O
events.description: S3 over RDMA transforms object storage from a capacity tier into an active capability layer for high performance computing. This session explores how RDMA removes the traditional performance limitations of S3-compatible storage, enabling high-throughput, low-overhead access for simulation, AI, analytics, checkpointing, and long-term data retention within a common storage architecture. NVIDIA will explain the technology behind the S3 over RDMA data path and present vendor testing demonstrating linear throughput scaling with 35 GB/s per node. Sandia National Laboratories will present independent laboratory testing conducted on earlier-generation hardware, providing an objective evaluation of the architecture and comparing those results with current vendor performance. Together, these perspectives illustrate how organizations can simplify data access, reduce unnecessary data movement between storage tiers, and enable a common S3 interface that supports modern hybrid HPC and AI workflows while improving scalability, operational efficiency, and infrastructure flexibility.

events.title: Tips and Traps: The Hidden Risks in Liquid Cooling Component Selection — and How To Avoid Them
events.description:
As data centers transition from air cooling to liquid cooling, many engineers are being tasked with designing fluid networks requiring new fluid-system knowledge. Selecting the wrong fluid transfer components can lead to long lead times, leaks, corrosion, performance issues, costly redesigns, and unplanned downtime.

This session will provide practical guidance on selecting and sourcing liquid cooling components for high performance computing and AI infrastructure. Topics include purpose-built component selection, fluid compatibility, dissimilar metals, leak prevention, attachment methods, pressure ratings, cleanliness requirements, manufacturability, flow dynamics, and quality traceability.

Attendees will gain a deeper understanding of the critical building blocks of liquid cooling systems and learn how to avoid common mistakes that can jeopardize reliability and system performance. Whether you're developing direct-to-chip cooling solutions or scaling data center infrastructure, this presentation will help your team make more informed and confident design decisions.

events.title: RT-HiSS: Ray Tracing Accelerated High-Dimensional Vector Similarity Searches
events.description: Recent GPU generations include special-purpose ray tracing (RT) cores for graphics applications. While RT cores are primarily used for rendering, recent works show they can be leveraged for general-purpose tasks, including similarity searches. However, existing approaches do not support datasets exceeding three dimensions. In this work, we propose RT-HiSS, the first exact GPU RT-core-based similarity search algorithm for high-dimensional datasets. GPU similarity search often scales poorly for large datasets with substantial search distances. To address this, RT-HiSS uses RT cores for fast index construction and searches, followed by candidate refinement on CUDA cores. We introduce a two-pass approach to estimate an upper bound on result size, enabling efficient batching under GPU memory constraints with near-perfect load balancing. Additionally, we examine shared memory tiling and compressed result masks to improve GPU resource utilization. RT-HiSS yields speedups up to 8.37x over competitive state-of-the-art GPU algorithms across six real-world datasets.

events.title: HolyDiver: Water and Carbon Footprint-Aware Serverless Computing
events.description: This paper introduces HolyDiver, a serverless function scheduling and execution strategy that jointly optimizes the carbon footprint, water footprint, and service time of serverless functions. HolyDiver is the first system to navigate the challenging three-way trade-off among these competing objectives by leveraging spatio-temporal variations in the environmental factors that impact the carbon and water footprint of electricity generation, datacenter operation, and cooling. To solve this optimization problem, HolyDiver demonstrates a novel application of Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) and extends HHO with dynamic hawk count adjustment, water scarcity-aware scheduling, and peer-guided performance estimation to adapt to the rapidly changing environmental conditions and function invocation patterns inherent to serverless environments. HolyDiver is evaluated on a cluster of nodes distributed across 10 regions with production-grade function execution traces and established benchmarks. We observe that HolyDiver consistently approaches the optimal solution and can complement existing schedulers to reduce the environmental footprint of serverless computing.

events.title: Unleashing Shared Memory Potential for NEP Machine-Learning Potential in Molecular Dynamics on GPUs
events.description:
Machine-learning potentials (MLPs) achieve near first-principles accuracy in molecular dynamics while retaining high efficiency. The neuroevolution potential (NEP) uses compact networks to deliver substantially higher GPU throughput than other MLPs. However, existing NEP implementations suffer from high per-thread memory demands that limit effective use of low-latency shared memory.

We present a shared-memory-centric optimization framework for NEP on GPUs. By introducing subwarp partitioning and two-dimensional neighbor reordering, it enhances inter-thread data sharing and reduces memory requirements, allowing most accesses to be served from shared memory. We further incorporate shared-memory-based matricized computation, buffering strategies, along with a series of GPU performance optimizations, and quantify shared memory usage to facilitate analysis.

Our framework achieves up to 18.09x speedup over the baseline GPU implementation and an average of 2.60x speedup over GPUMD across five representative material systems on NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

events.title: MIST: A Co-Design Framework for Heterogeneous, Multi-Stage LLM Inference
events.description:
Modern LLM serving spans multi-stage pipelines, including RAG retrieval and KV cache reuse, with distinct compute, memory, and latency demands. Inference engines expose vast configuration spaces with no systematic navigation methodology, and exhaustive benchmarking can exceed $40K in cloud costs. Meanwhile, hardware is diversifying across AMD GPUs, TPUs, and custom ASICs, yet cross-vendor prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation lacks a unified software stack for end-to-end evaluation. We present MIST, an event-driven simulation framework that models the full serving stack across AI workload, system and software, and hardware layers, with pluggable accelerator models enabling cross-vendor evaluation. MIST achieves end-to-end fidelity within 6% of real deployed systems. In design-space exploration case studies, under stated pricing and hardware assumptions, multi-vendor PD-disaggregated deployments identified by MIST yield up to 49.3% higher tokens/$ than single-vendor PD disaggregation. MIST also enables KV storage co-design, revealing how memory hierarchy choices shape tail latency.

MIST is available at https://github.com/MIST-Simulator/MIST.

events.title: Prefill-Decode Aggregation or Disaggregation? Unifying Both for Goodput-Optimized LLM Serving
events.description:
Large language model (LLM) serving has long centered on a debate between prefill-decode (PD) aggregation and disaggregation. We systematically compare them under joint time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT) service-level objectives (SLOs): aggregation wins when TTFT SLOs are tight and TPOT SLOs relaxed; disaggregation wins in the opposite regime. Under balanced SLOs, however, both are significantly suboptimal in SLO-compliant throughput (goodput), revealing a previously uncharacterized gap.

We attribute this gap to unexploited latency slack: many requests complete well within SLOs while others approach violation. We propose latency shifting, a design principle for reallocating SLO slack across requests and phases to maximize goodput. TaiChi, an LLM serving system, unifies aggregation and disaggregation through hybrid-mode inference to realize this principle through flowing decode and length-aware prefill scheduling. TaiChi improves goodput by up to 40% and reduces P90 TTFT and TPOT by up to 5.3× and 1.6×, respectively, over state-of-the-art aggregation and disaggregation systems.

events.title: What Is Quantum and Why Should One Care?
events.description:
Dr. Prem Kumar will take attendees inside the rapidly emerging world of Quantum 2.0, showing why quantum networking could fundamentally change how we communicate and connect. He will reveal how quantum and classical networks can work together — and showcase his group’s breakthrough work with a live SC26 demonstration at the Ciena booth, where attendees can watch quantum entanglement travel alongside real internet traffic.

Dr. Kumar promises a glimpse of what the quantum internet could look like — and how we might build it.

events.title: Agentic WAN‑Native LLM Orchestration: From User‑Driven Inference to Geographically Distributed Model Instances Across Internet2, PNRP, and SCinet via NRP and SENSE
events.description: SENSE-NRI(TomL), CalTech-NRI(HarveyN), StarLight-NRI(JoeM)

events.title: The KV Cache Is the New Hot Tier: Storage Architecture for Persistent Context in Large-Scale AI Inference
events.description: Inference has inverted the AI storage problem. Reasoning models and agentic workloads generate KV caches far larger than GPU memory, and every eviction can lead to expensive prefill recomputation that inflates time to first token and wastes accelerator cycles. This talk presents a storage architecture that treats persisted context as a first-class tier in a parallel file system: node-local SSD managed as a coherent buffer under a global namespace, DMA and RDMA transport that minimizes copying, asynchronous chunked KV cache writeback with managed persistence, access-pattern-driven tiering for context and retrieval data, and distributed metadata for high-concurrency small-object access. We examine when persistence beats recomputation, flash endurance under cache-writeback load, and early performance characterization, with sizing guidance for facilities serving training and inference on shared infrastructure and opportunities to improve non-AI storage performance.

events.title: Design for Decades: The Engineering Truth About HPC Hardware Lifespans
events.description:
As governments, universities, and enterprises scale HPC and AI data center infrastructure, long-term hardware reliability is a critical requirement for mission-critical applications. HPC liquid cooling systems are expected to operate continuously for years under demanding thermal and mechanical conditions. By combining predictive material modeling with accelerated life testing and real-world deployment data, engineers can make more informed decisions about design, reliability, maintenance intervals, and long-term system performance.

An AQS certified senior reliability engineer will present research focused on predicting service life, using quick disconnects (QDs) in liquid cooling systems as an example. Designed for engineers, the session will examine how techniques such as advanced creep modeling and accelerated life testing (ALT) are used to predict long-term material performance under continuous thermal and mechanical stress.

Attendees will review examples demonstrating how operating temperature, applied stress, and material selection impact projected service life, along with a real-world case study for a U.S. national laboratory.

events.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Scientific Particle Data Compression and Rendering
events.description: Large-scale particle simulations produce hundreds of millions of particles, straining storage, transfer, and interactive visualization. Existing lossy compressors such as SZ3 operate in data space and provide no guarantees on downstream visualization fidelity. We propose ParticleGS, a visualization-aware framework based on 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that learns a compact representation directly optimized for rendered image quality, combining (1) a multi-stage, multi-orbit training pipeline, (2) VizMapper, a lightweight network that adapts a single trained model to user-specified visualization parameters at inference time, and (3) spatial block training with KD-tree decomposition and global fine-tuning. On a 281-million-particle HACC cosmological simulation, our eight-block model reaches 30.03 dB PSNR at 65× compression, outperforming SZ3 by 5–8 dB at comparable ratios, and generalizes without tuning to additional HACC regions and a dark-matter-only FIRE-2 simulation. It renders at 662 FPS on a single GPU, over 2,300× faster than ParaView on the full particle data.

events.title: Policy-Constrained Delegated Access for HPC
events.description: High performance computing systems rely on a direct user-access model: users authenticate at the access boundary and operate within Unix accounts. This model supports strong attribution and bounded privilege but does not address the growing role of software that accesses clusters on behalf of users. Science gateways, workflow systems, and remote development tools initiate SSH-mediated actions without per-connection user involvement. Existing delegation mechanisms such as shared credentials and long-lived keys weaken auditability and complicate enforcement. This paper treats delegated cluster access as an access-control problem at the HPC access boundary. We present a policy-constrained signer that validates the user's identity, maps requests to site-defined Unix principals, and issues short-lived SSH certificates scoped by policy. Standard OpenSSH login nodes enforce these certificates with no additional software. We evaluate the signer on a Jetstream2 SLURM testbed across issuance overhead, enforcement, revocation, and auditability. We separately evaluate certificate-based workflow resilience under connection drops.

events.title: Every Microsecond Matters: Achieving Near-Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives
events.description: GPU collective communication is often optimized for bandwidth, yet many emerging workloads are latency-bound. Long-context LLM inference is a key example, where small collectives lie on the critical path of token generation, making microsecond-scale overheads impactful. In this work, we study how to approach the hardware speed-of-light (SoL) lower bound for GPU collectives within a scale-up network. We identify key design principles, including barrier-free synchronization and efficient use of symmetric memory and multicast. Building on NCCL’s device-side API, we develop low-latency interfaces for constructing custom kernels and implement new symmetric collectives in NCCL. Microbenchmarks show substantial latency reductions, achieving within 10% of the measured SoL bound. Integrated into applications, these kernels reduce inter-token latency and improve throughput in LLM inference, while also accelerating cuSOLVERMp, demonstrating benefits across AI and HPC workloads.

events.title: BidKV: Utility-Guided Preemption Scheduling for KV-Pressure LLM Serving
events.description:
When key-value (KV) cache demand exceeds GPU memory in online large language model (LLM) serving, engines reclaim active requests' cache. Poor victim selection increases recomputation and time to first token (TTFT). We present BidKV, a utility-guided policy that ranks victims by recoverable capacity and estimated disruption cost. BidKV integrates with vLLM and SGLang through a portable adapter that reuses native preemption. With Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and ShareGPT traces, BidKV reduces 95th-percentile TTFT by over 90% and improves 300 ms service-level objective (SLO) attainment by 14.8 percentage points over vLLM's native policy. On SGLang, it reduces 95th-percentile TTFT by 94.6% and improves SLO attainment by 38.8 percentage points over native least-recently-used eviction.

Source code is available at https://github.com/CGCL-codes/BidKV.

events.title: Papers in Conversation
events.description: About Papers in Conversation: Each session highlights three technical papers addressing a common or emerging HPC topic. Following the paper presentations, a 20-minute moderated panel discussion will explore connections among the papers, contrasting perspectives, broader implications, open challenges, and future research directions. Our goal is to go beyond the individual contributions and encourage a conversation that helps the audience understand the larger research landscape, including where the field might be heading.

events.title: Global Network Advancement Group Data Intensive Science WG
Regional Tech Hub Meet and Greet: Becky Gillespie
Applications, Libraries, and Tools in Modern Fortran (alt.fortran)
events.description: Fortran plays a crucial role in numerous applications. This BoF provides a forum for Fortran developers to engage with the language's modern programming features. With features introduced in recent language revisions, Fortran 2023 supports modern programming practices and high performance computing (HPC). This BoF gathers developers from diverse domains to share experiences and explore Fortran's evolving capabilities. After some brief presentations, the session will focus on an interactive discussion where audience members will be encouraged to share their own experiences and ask questions of our experts.

events.title: Correctness Testing of HPC Scientific Software in the Age of AI-Generated Code
events.description: Effective software testing plays a critical role in guaranteeing the performance, correctness, and reproducibility of software. Testing high-performance computing (HPC) software poses unique challenges due to massive parallelism, concurrency and heterogeneity, the scale of target platforms, lack of oracles, and application-specific verification and verification. These challenges are now amplified by AI coding tools generating and translating HPC code faster than humans can review it. In this BoF, a panel of experts and the audience will discuss methodologies and challenges in HPC software testing, including verification of AI-generated code to deepen our understanding of this crucial aspect of HPC software development.

events.title: Communication Libraries in HPC and AI
events.description: The world's largest supercomputers for scientific discovery are also premier systems for artificial intelligence model training and inference. While traditional HPC compute has predominately leveraged the MPI standard, AI workloads have increasingly focused on collective communication libraries, such as NVIDIA's NCCL and AMD's RCCL, which are optimized for high throughput and GPU-native usage. This Birds of a Feather (BoF) session at the SC Conference (SC) aims to delve into the intricacies of collective communication libraries, focusing on the comparison between the widely adopted Message Passing Interface (MPI) and NCCL/RCCL, as well as other key messaging libraries, such as SHMEM.

events.title: Open OnDemand User Group Meeting
events.description: This BoF is meant to be an open discussion to guide the future roadmap for Open OnDemand (openondemand.org), by getting feedback from the community on the prioritization of the various tasks planned for the next few years. OOD is extremely relevant to ongoing discussions within the HPC community about user interfaces and science gateways. The session leaders, all part of the OOD development team, will jointly develop the content for the presentation in advance to ensure a wide range of viewpoints and topics are presented. We will also consult with our user advisory group in advance for their suggestions.

events.title: HPC Developments for Fusion Energy Applications
events.description: The growing interest in fusion energy to power massive data centers has created an urgent need to accelerate plasma science codes. Both experimental capabilities and computational workflows are complex and often render current technologies inefficient, which results in a severe lack of data. Implementation of plasma codes becomes complicated due to variations in software and hardware architectures. A potential solution is to develop an abstraction layer to connect infrastructure to application codes. This BoF focuses on identifying the needs for development and standardization of an abstraction layer, and the relevant functionalities/data structures that would be most useful to abstract.

events.title: One Year After MPI 5.0: Impact and What's Next?
events.description: The Message Passing Interface (MPI) API is the most dominant programming approach for HPC environments. Its specification is driven by the MPI Forum, an open forum consisting of MPI developers, vendors, and users. This year, the MPI Forum published the latest version of the standard, MPI 5.0. We will take a look at the new features and will discuss what they mean for the users of MPI. We will also discuss ongoing work toward the next version of the MPI standard, with lightning talks from the working groups, and get feedback from the community.

events.title: Autonomous Science Network: A Grassroots Community for Trustworthy Science
events.description: Autonomous experiment operation is demonstrating the ability to dramatically improve the pace of scientific discovery. This BoF convenes a community to continue building on the early two-year roadmap, discussing how different teams are using agentic workflows to improve the potential for new discovery and to address the related need to verify the new results.

events.title: Operational Data Analytics: Agentic AI for HPC Facilities
events.description: Operational data analytics (ODA) has become essential for understanding and optimizing HPC systems. However, converting the vast amounts of operational data they generate into actionable insights still requires significant manual effort and domain expertise. Agentic AI has the potential to extend traditional analytics by reading telemetry, correlating signals, diagnosing problems, and drafting fixes for an operator to approve. This BoF will explore the state of the art in agentic AI’s applicability to ODA, promising use cases, limitations, and governance challenges. Participants will share experiences and discuss how agentic AI can enhance future HPC operations and efficiency.

events.title: IO500: The High-Performance Storage Community
events.description: The IO500 is the de facto benchmark standard for HPC storage. Official IO500 lists have been released at ISC and SC events since SC17 and now have over 300 entries. The purpose is to foster the high-performance storage community and ensure forward progress towards the common goals of creating, sharing, and benefiting from a large corpus of shared storage data. IO500 also serves as the largest repository of detailed HPC storage information for researchers and system designers to analyze and evaluate over time. A key BoF highlight is the presentation of the latest IO500 Production and Research lists.

events.title: Photonics for AI and HPC: Breaking the Bandwidth and Power Barrier
events.description: As AI and HPC systems scale to unprecedented levels, traditional electrical interconnects are becoming a limiting factor. Silicon photonics offers a promising path to address bandwidth, energy efficiency and interconnect scalability constraints, but questions remain around deployment readiness, integration complexity and ecosystem maturity. Led by industry analyst Dan Olds, this session brings together experts from Penguin Solutions, Marvell and Micron to explore photonic interconnects from multiple perspectives. Panelists will discuss the technology’s value today, the technical and operational challenges ahead, where photonics can make the greatest impact, and what the broader ecosystem must do to accelerate real-world adoption.
events.scheduleTitle: Photonics for AI and HPC Clusters: Breaking the Bandwidth and Power Barrier

events.title: Navigating Complexity: Achieving Performance Portability in the Evolving Landscape of Accelerated HPC Systems
events.description: With the increasing demand for AI in HPC, there has been a rapid rise in accelerated architectures, portable programming models, and frameworks. The already-daunting task of programming for interconnected accelerated systems has become even more complex. This BoF, organized by IXPUG, will focus on portable programming across a wide range of heterogeneous architectures—including Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, and ARM supporting diverse simulation, data analytics, and AI workloads. The session will explore key challenges, state-of-the-art solutions, and emerging best practices for programming across these systems, identifying common principles and methodologies that support development and long-term maintenance across sites, architectures, and scientific applications.

events.title: A Single Pane of Glass for AI Supercomputing: Interoperable Access Portals Worldwide
events.description: Providing simplified access to distributed HPC, AI, and cloud resources is a global challenge. Driven by major investments and user demand for a single pane of glass, the need for interoperable resource portals is clear—yet implementations that work across institutional and national boundaries remain hard. Following a well-received ISC 2026 BoF, this session broadens the conversation to operators of federated research infrastructures across Europe, the U.S., and Asia-Pacific, sharing experiences, challenges overcome, and lessons learned. Through lightning updates, live polling, and moderated discussion, attendees exchange practical approaches to federated identity, allocation, accounting, and site autonomy versus federated consistency.

events.title: How Must HPC Education Change for a World Where AI Generates Our Code?
events.description: In the near future (if not already) HPC software will be generated by AI. The question is not “if” we must adapt, but “how” we will adapt. Everything about our software will be impacted. In this BoF, we will focus on training: How does what we teach have to change to accommodate the necessary shift in skills in the AI era? We need ideas from across the community and people who will dedicate the time to debate these ideas, digest them, and produce a position paper to drive the change we need in HPC. It all starts with this BoF.

events.title: Unified Communication X (UCX) Community
events.description:
In order to exploit the capabilities of new HPC systems and to meet their demands in scalability, communication software needs to scale to millions of cores and support applications with adequate functionality. UCX is a collaboration between industry, national labs, and academia that consolidates and provides a unified open-source framework.

The UCX project is managed by the UCF Consortium (http://www.ucfconsortium.org/). The session will serve as the UCX community meeting and will introduce the latest developments to HPC developers and the broader user community.

events.title: Talking to Your Users: Ask Better Questions Before You Build
events.description: User experience (UX) is often misunderstood as a nice-to-have, rather than a necessary element of scientific computing. In reality, UX encompasses all the ways a user interacts with a product and is highly relevant to HPC systems. This interactive BoF will introduce UX work as a practical approach for improving usability and adoption. Participants will discuss how to ask users better questions to uncover needs and identify opportunities to improve systems, services, and support. Participants will leave with practical methods, starter resources, and connections to a growing cross-institutional UX community. This session benefits developers, documentation specialists, and facility support staff.

events.title: OpenQSE: Building an Open Quantum-HPC Software Ecosystem
events.description: Quantum computing resources are increasingly integrated into HPC and cloud environments, but software stacks remain isolated, vendor-specific, and often proprietary. OpenQSE is a community effort developing an open, modular ecosystem of vendor-neutral specifications to close the interoperability gaps that fragment hybrid quantum-classical workflows. This BoF will briefly share the initiative's roadmap and working-group progress, then open the floor for structured discussion with HPC facility staff, application teams, vendors, and researchers to identify priorities and shape the direction together. The intended outcome is a prioritized set of integration artifacts the community identifies as most urgent for near-term development.

events.title: Regional Tech Hub Meet and Greet: Bob Grossman
events.description: Robert L. Grossman, PhD, is the Frederick H. Rawson Distinguished Service Professor in Medicine and Computer Science and the Jim and Karen Frank Director of the Center for Translational Data Science at the University of Chicago. He joined the faculty in 2010 and served as the chief research informatics officer (CRIO) of the Biological Sciences Division from 2011-2024. He is also the Chief of the Section of Biomedical Data Science in the Department of Medicine. He is the principal investigator for the National Cancer Institute Genomic Data Commons (GDC), a platform for the cancer research community that manages, analyzes, integrates, and shares large-scale genomic datasets in support of precision medicine. The GDC is used by more than 150,000 researchers each month. He has also built data commons to support research in other areas, including cardiovascular diseases, infectious diseases and medical imaging. His research interests include data science, AI, and machine learning. He is the founder and a partner at Analytic Strategy Partners, which helps companies develop AI strategies, and a Director of the Open Commons Consortium (OCC), which is a not-for-profit that manages and operates data commons and data meshes to advance scientific and biomedical research. He served as a member of the NOAA Scientific Advisory Board (SAB) from 2017-2024 and as a member of the Frederick National Laboratory Advisory Committee (FNLAC) from 2014-2021. He earned his PhD in applied mathematics at Princeton University and an AB in mathematics from Harvard University.

events.title: Network-Enabled Transcontinental CryoEM Over AmLight and FABRIC
Double-Precision Matrix Multiplication Emulation via Ozaki-II Scheme with FP8 Quantization
events.description: In this paper, we propose a method for emulating double-precision general matrix–matrix multiplication (DGEMM), a fundamental and performance-critical kernel in many high-performance computing applications. Ozaki-I and Ozaki-II are established DGEMM emulation schemes via low-precision matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) units. For the Ozaki-I scheme, INT8-, FP8-, and FP16-based implementations have been proposed, all of which can be realized based on the same underlying algorithmic structure. In contrast, although INT8-based implementations of the Ozaki-II scheme have been reported, the original algorithm cannot be directly adapted to exploit FP8 MMA units. In several recent architectures, such as NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra and NVIDIA Rubin, INT8 performance has been reduced, making reliance on INT8 alone insufficient. Therefore, we introduce a novel technique to demonstrate DGEMM emulation based on the Ozaki-II scheme that operates on FP8 MMA units. Compared to the FP8-based Ozaki-I scheme, our method significantly reduces the computational cost and enables efficient FP64 emulation.

events.title: Precision Engineering for Matrix Computation
events.description: These papers use emulation, quantization, analytical modeling, and mixed precision to reshape matrix computation. The session focuses on recovering scientific accuracy while exploiting modern accelerator formats.

events.title: Compression and Communication for Data-Intensive HPC
events.description: The papers show how compression, sparsity, and communication co-design reduce data movement: extreme generative compression for Earth observation, communication-optimized distributed diffusion inference, sparsity-aware GPU collectives, and compressed/homomorphic MPI collectives.

events.title: hZCCL2: Co-Designing Collective Communication with Vectorized Homomorphic Compression
events.description: Inter-node collective communication is a dominant bottleneck in large-scale scientific simulations and distributed artificial-intelligence workloads. Prior frameworks mitigate this via error-bounded lossy compression but face fundamental limits: scalar encoding underutilizes memory bandwidth, and outliers inflate fixed-length blocks, leaving compression ratio (CR) untapped at SIMD-friendly block sizes. We present hZCCL2, a co-designed framework that optimizes SIMD encoding, homomorphic compression, and collective communication. Its HVZ compressor achieves up to 5.31x higher compression throughput than prior state-of-the-art compressors and improves CR by up to 37.6% at SIMD-friendly block sizes with outlier-aware encoding. Its homomorphic compression is up to 8.1x faster than the decompress-operate-compress workflow. Evaluated on 3,584 CPU cores, hZCCL2 reaches up to 47.2x Bcast, 23.4x Scatter, 43.8x Allreduce, and 67.6x Alltoall peak speedups over native MPI. In an image-stacking application, it achieves 12.9x speedup at a single thread and 39.5x at 112 threads while preserving the user-specified error bound.

events.title: Best Papers: Scalable and Elastic AI Systems
events.description: These papers address dynamic sparsity, out-of-core training, and serverless execution for modern AI workloads. Together they show how software abstractions can make increasingly irregular models scalable and usable.

events.title: DySpin: A Plug-and-Play Library Advancing Dynamic Sparse Long-Context Inference
events.description: Long-context LLM inference is constrained by the memory-bandwidth and capacity demands of the key-value (KV) cache. Existing sparse methods typically use fixed per-head token budgets, overlooking variations in runtime demand. Moreover, since they retain all tokens in memory, these methods do not alleviate GPU memory capacity constraints. To overcome these limitations, we present DySpin, a plug-and-play library for dynamic sparse long-context inference. Its training-free runtime allocator dynamically adjusts token budgets to preserve important tokens and improve accuracy. To address the resulting workload imbalance, FastEstimate fuses token-importance evaluation and selection to generate scheduling indices that guide a specialized decoding attention kernel for fine-grained load balancing. DySpin further employs six-bit KV cache quantization and a novel packing format that enables register-level parallel unpacking and dequantization, reducing both dequantization overhead and memory footprint. DySpin integrates with existing sparse frameworks, improving accuracy while reducing long-context inference latency and KV cache memory usage.

events.title: FluidGPU: Fine-Grained Kernel Disaggregation for Large Model Inference on Heterogeneous GPUs
events.description: This paper presents FluidGPU, the first kernel disaggregation system to improve performance and cost efficiency on heterogeneous GPUs for large model inference. Our key insight is that kernels within a single application exhibit diverse resource demands, making them the most suitable granularity for aligning computation with hardware capabilities. FluidGPU integrates offline analysis with online adaptation by extracting precise inter-kernel dependencies from PTX to ensure correctness, overlapping communication with computation through a pipelined execution model, and employing workload-aware scheduling with lightweight runtime adaptation. Extensive evaluations across five heterogeneous GPUs and four model architectures, scaling up to 16 GPUs, show that FluidGPU improves serving throughput and cost efficiency by up to 2.3× and 1.6×, respectively, compared to existing disaggregation methods, while generalizing to model architectures where prior approaches do not apply. Surprisingly, a heterogeneous GPU pair under FluidGPU can even exceed the throughput of two homogeneous high-end GPUs at a lower cost.

events.title: LLM Systems: Inference, Agents, and HPC Operations
events.description: These papers treat large models as both HPC workloads and components of intelligent HPC systems: heterogeneous-GPU inference, distributed agent scheduling, LLM-assisted HPC job management, and low-overhead fault tolerance for zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning.

events.title: Evaluation and Optimization of Communication Compression for 10K-GPU LLM Training
events.description: Collective communication is critical for scaling large language model (LLM) training to megascale GPU clusters. However, communication becomes a major bottleneck limiting scalability. Existing approaches improve bandwidth utilization but are constrained by the physical network in large-scale clusters. Communication compression reduces data volume and offers a way to break the communication wall, yet its performance and accuracy at extreme scale remain unclear. To bridge this gap, we present the first systematic study of communication compression across scales up to 10K GPUs, showing that it maintains accuracy but suffers from limited performance gains due to bandwidth hierarchy limitations, weak communication scaling, and limited resource awareness. We enhance the co-design of communication and compression with a hierarchical method that restructures communication compression, adapts communication algorithms to each scale, and tunes network resource allocation. Our approach achieves up to 5.87x communication improvement and 1.73x end-to-end training speedup on Llama3 models at 10,240 GPUs.

events.title: Papers in Conversation: Moving AI at Scale: Networks, Collectives, and Compression
events.description: These papers connect compressed collectives, hyperscale network design, and evidence from 10,000-GPU training. They frame communication as the central scaling challenge for frontier AI systems.

events.title: The 50-State AI Plan: A Grassroots Approach to Building a US AI Continent
events.description: This session examines how state and regional initiatives can strengthen U.S. leadership in AI and quantum computing. Using Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Utah, Oklahoma, and others as examples, the panel will explore how states are aligning regional assets with America’s AI Action Plan, the Genesis Mission, and the National AI Research Resource (NAIRR). The discussion frames this work as a grassroots U.S. counterpart to the EU “AI Continent,” built through state-led, place-based innovation rather than a top-down model. Building on the NSF-CASC Workshop on Envisioning NAIRR State and Regional Hubs for Educational Transformation, the session will highlight pathways for expanding workforce development, research access, and regional cooperation. Panelists will discuss partnerships among academia, government, industry, philanthropy, and federal agencies, along with strategies for broadening access to computing and data resources, streamlining deployment, and engaging states in AI capacity building. Inclusive state-led hubs can drive innovation, attract investment, and grow the AI workforce.

events.title: The 50-State AI Plan: A Grassroots Approach to Building a US AI Continent
Unleashing Performance: How CXL and Disaggregated Memory Are Revolutionizing HPC and AI
events.description:
As memory-bound workloads begin to dominate HPC and AI, traditional architectures face severe limitations in memory bandwidth and capacity. Compute Express Link® (CXL®) is providing the means to create disaggregated and composable memory tiers to accelerate HPC and AI performance.

This panel, moderated by Dan Olds, features experts from Penguin Solutions, SemiconDx, and Intel, who will explore the evolving role of CXL in next-generation HPC/AI systems. Panelists will discuss emerging memory architectures, performance benchmarks, cost and scale trade-offs, alongside lessons learned from early implementations and incorporation of emerging technologies, such as silicon photonics, that should be on everyone’s roadmap.

Through interactive discussion and audience engagement, the session will highlight real-world benchmarks discussing CXL-enabled systems, as well as practical insights into memory-constrained workloads. Attendees will understand current limitations, gain actionable guidance, and leave better equipped to evaluate and resolve memory constraints in HPC and AI environments.

events.title: Unleashing Performance: How CXL and Disaggregated Memory Are Revolutionizing HPC and AI
Best Poster Finalist Presentations (ACM SRC Undergrads)
Beyond NVQLink: Entanglement-Based Interconnects for Quantum Computing Scale-Out
events.description: Quantum is becoming a key component of future HPC strategies either in stand-alone or specialized accelerator roles. However, connectivity of these systems in a way that preserves the quantum state remains outside of the ability of today’s classical interconnects. While advancements such as NVIDIA NVQLink are vital in connecting classical systems to quantum resources, they can’t carry quantum information between QPUs. This session outlines why quantum systems can’t cluster on classical networks, contrasts the role of hybrid interconnects (such as NVQlink) to native quantum links needed for scaling quantum resources, and the role of photonic quantum links in that process. It introduces the hardware/software stack needed to create quantum clusters, including quantum network interfaces, quantum memories, photonic switching, and compilation software in this paradigm. Attendees will learn the components of a quantum-enabled HPC cluster, how to plan for integration, and lay out a scale-out-based strategy that includes quantum.

events.title: Quantum Computing II
The Mission Continues: Veteran Voices in SC26
events.description: Active-duty servicemen and veterans are part of the workforce in high performance computing (HPC). This panel features speakers with a broad range of experience in HPC who will discuss strategies and leveraging training and skills, and how it translates into working in industry, academia and national laboratories.

events.title: The Mission Continues: Veteran Voices in SC26
HPC Power and Cooling II
Improving Rack Manifold Integration with Self-Aligning Blindmate Couplings
events.description: Rack-level liquid cooling places increasing demands on blindmate coupling performance, especially as manifold layouts become more compact and component density increases. This session examines the evolution from traditional floating block mechanisms to self-aligning blindmate coupling designs with integrated misalignment capability. The discussion will focus on how newer approaches support larger offsets, reduce the impact of hose routing forces, improve flow efficiency, and allow couplings to recenter during operation. Using rack manifold applications, including the AMD Helios, the presentation will highlight practical design considerations for engineers specifying fluid conveyance components in dense liquid-cooled compute systems.

events.title: Regional Tech Hub: Biomedical
events.description:
The emerging clinical actionability of multimodal AI — from understanding medical images and clinical context to using AI-generated insights to guide treatment decisions.

Together, the talks showcase two complementary applications of multimodal AI: HOPPR’s foundation models are expanding how AI interprets medical images alongside clinical information, while Dr. Pearson’s work explores how AI-derived pathology biomarkers can translate those insights into treatment decisions.

events.title: When Pixels Speak: Foundation Models in Medical Imaging
events.description:
In his talk, Dr. Siddiqui will explain how multimodal vision language models, or VLMs, are changing the practice of radiology, spanning everything from feature detection in medical images to interpreting complex clinical information. It also will explore how artificial intelligence is supporting radiologists throughout the workflow, including image analysis and draft report generation.

Dr. Siddiqui promises a closer look at what these technologies mean for the future of radiology and patient care.

events.title: Network-Enabled Transcontinental CryoEM Over AmLight and FABRIC
EmuGEMM: Fused Tensor Core Kernels for Precision Emulation in Matrix Multiplication
events.description:
Modern GPUs devote an increasing silicon budget to low-precision matrix-multiplication units, widening the precision–throughput gap for scientific computing workloads. Ozaki Schemes I and II offer an alternative by reconstructing high-precision general matrix multiplication (GEMM) from low-precision operations, yet existing implementations leave substantial performance untapped. In particular, intermediate results are repeatedly materialized in global memory, making data movement the dominant bottleneck.

We present EmuGEMM, fused integer Tensor Core kernels for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that eliminate redundant memory round-trips in both Ozaki schemes. Using Scheme I, EmuGEMM sustains up to 1,639 Top/s on Hopper (83% of INT8 peak) and 3,654 Top/s on Blackwell (81%). For large matrices, EmuGEMM surpasses cuBLAS TF32 throughput by up to 1.4× on Hopper and 1.7× on Blackwell, at comparable accuracy. Using Scheme II, EmuGEMM extends to complex arithmetic and outperforms cuBLAS ZGEMM by up to 2.3× on Hopper and 5.5× on Blackwell.

events.title: Scaling Spatiotemporal Generative Compression for Earth Observation on an HPC-AI-Converged Supercomputer
events.description: Earth observation constellations generate multispectral data at unprecedented rates, creating storage and distribution bottlenecks. To reduce storage and accelerate global dissemination, we propose a scalable two-stage generative compression framework validated on annual global Sentinel-2 imagery. The encoding stage exploits large-scale spatial context and temporal redundancy, while the reconstruction stage restores the multispectral latent space and uses geolocation and observation time as metadata controls to guide generation with global historical priors. To meet the computational and memory demands of training global-scale generative models, we redesign the framework for an HPC-AI-converged supercomputer. Through topology-aware hierarchical parallelization, asymmetric HBM-DDR memory placement, and asynchronous overlap execution on Armv9 and SME, our implementation achieves end-to-end training performance comparable to high-end A100 GPU platforms under the reported workload and scales to 20,480 LineShine nodes with 76% weak-scaling efficiency. It achieves over 4,700x archive compression, outperforming existing compression methods in downstream land-cover classification.

events.title: SwarmLoRA: Serverless Shared-Computation Disaggregation for Isolated, High-Throughput Multi-LoRA Serving
events.description: Over 100,000 public LoRA adapters now share a small number of base LLMs, and cloud providers increasingly serve them for independent tenants whose private data must stay isolated. Serverful systems co-locate all adapters in one process for efficient batching but sacrifice isolation; serverless systems run each adapter in an isolated function but redundantly recompute the shared base-model projection in every one, wasting GPU memory bandwidth. We present SwarmLoRA, a disaggregated serverless architecture that separates shared computation from per-adapter state. A persistent aggregator batches the base-model projection once across all active functions; isolated worker functions each hold one adapter’s weights and KV cache and scale independently. This design achieves cross-adapter batching without breaking per-adapter isolation. SwarmLoRA achieves 4.1×-4.9× higher throughput on four L40S GPUs than state-of-the-art ServerlessLLM and ServerlessLoRA, while preventing cross-tenant data leakage through malicious adapters. SwarmLoRA shows that multi-tenant LoRA serving need not trade tenant isolation for batching efficiency.

events.title: How Much Can Large Language Models Optimize Job Management in HPC Systems？
events.description: Large language models are increasingly capable, yet their integration into HPC job management remains limited. This paper identifies three optimization opportunities across the job lifecycle: resource demand prediction at submission, adaptive backfill parameter reconfiguration during scheduling, and anomaly diagnosis during execution. We build a unified framework combining domain-specific supervised fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic workflows, and further incorporate rigorous hallucination mitigation mechanisms to ensure safe and reliable deployment. Extensive experiments on multiple open-source and proprietary LLMs using several historical datasets demonstrate that our domain-specific models can consistently improve job resource demand prediction accuracy, enhance scheduling efficiency via online reconfiguration of backfill parameters, and provide interpretable root-cause triage through a dual-agent workflow. Ultimately, this work establishes a foundational step toward intelligent HPC environments.

events.title: RailX: A Flexible, Scalable, and Low-Cost Network Architecture for Hyper-Scale AI Workloads
events.description: The exponential growth of AI models necessitates hyper-scale networking infrastructures with unprecedented cost-effectiveness and scalability. However, traditional packet-switched fat-trees are prohibitively expensive, while direct circuit-switched topologies exhibit poor scalability and limited all-to-all performance. In this paper, we present a novel reconfigurable network architecture called RailX that achieves high scalability, high performance, high flexibility, and low cost simultaneously. RailX organizes nodes and optical switches in a 2D configuration, achieving much better scalability than existing centralized circuit switching networks. We propose a novel interconnection method based on Hamiltonian decomposition theory to organize separate rail-based rings into all-to-all topologies, simultaneously optimizing both ring-collective and all-to-all communication at ultra-scale. RailX's flat switching layer interconnects over 400K high-bandwidth chips with a diameter of just 2-4 inter-node hops. It slashes costs per all-reduce and all-to-all bandwidth to under 10% and 50% of fat-trees, respectively. For MLaaS, we flexibly map diverse AI workloads and bypass hardware failures.

events.title: Quantum Safe Networking — QKD — Any Attempt To Observe the Quantum Channel Leaves Evidence
events.description: No NRI

events.title: Regional Tech Hub Meet and Greet: Andrea Jett
Regional Tech Hub Meet and Greet: Avinash Maurya
Controlling Long-Lived Logical Qubits for QPU Integration Into HPC Centers
events.description: Quantum computers have shown theoretical promise, from quantum chemistry to prime number factoring, but they cannot deliver on that promise alone. Quantum processors (QPUs) will need to integrate with classical high performance computing (HPC) resources to reach their full potential. Ultimately, QPUs will become quantum accelerators within HPC centers, empowering users to solve new problems previously thought to be out of reach for classical computation. In the near-term, QPUs will leverage HPC computation for faster bring-up and recalibration as well as decoding quantum error correction (QEC) syndromes. Quantum control systems perform the essential role of bridging the gap between the classical world and quantum information. This presentation covers the latest advancements in the quantum computing control systems needed to control long-lived logical qubits for HPC integration: from individual hardware layers to software frameworks that allow for both low-level pulse control and high-level quantum circuit compilation.

events.title: Any Rack, Everywhere: Future-Readiness for the 800 VDC Transition
events.description:
The shift to 800 VDC is settled in direction but not in endpoint or path, and most operators don't know what IT loads they will need to serve. Future-ready means moving to ultra-high-density racks and some mix of 800 VDC without tearing apart the building or stranding resources. This session presents a framework built on two types of design decisions: hard-to-change infrastructure sized for future loads on day one, and flexible interfaces that let operators change what connects without rip-and-replace.
1) Setting a credible planning envelope for density and power
2) Four real-world transition scenarios, from a few DC racks in an AC pod to full DC conversion
3) Possibilities at the edge of what we know
The session concludes with a simple formula: future-ready equals hard-to-change infrastructure sized for future loads on day one, plus flexible interfaces that simplify the transition and provide options. Minimize stranded capacity. Minimize wasted capital. Minimize disruption.

events.title: DOLPHIN: Scalable Disk-RAM-GPU Pipelined Training for Massive Temporal GNNs
events.description:
Temporal graph neural networks (T-GNNs) play a key role in modeling dynamic graphs by learning representations that capture evolving structures and interactions.

However, scaling T-GNNs remains challenging, as massive real-world graphs and complex temporal dependencies incur prohibitive runtime and memory costs. Existing systems often preload entire datasets into RAM and rely on RAM-GPU pipelines, suffering from batch-boundary pipeline bubbles, thereby limiting throughput.

In this paper, we present DOLPHIN, a scalable Disk-RAM-GPU pipelined system for massive T-GNNs. DOLPHIN groups training batches into chunks and incorporates two key techniques: an I/O-efficient feature window scheduler for just-in-time Disk-to-RAM chunk provisioning, and a dependency-graph–based parallel execution plan that improves GPU utilization while preserving model quality. Together, these techniques improve pipeline efficiency across the Disk-RAM-GPU memory hierarchy and computation phases.

Experiments on six real-world graphs show DOLPHIN delivers up to 21.07x faster training and reduces RAM usage by up to 92.04% compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

events.title: Pushing the Limits of Structured Sparse GEMM on Hopper GPUs via Analytical Modeling
events.description: Structured sparsity improves performance in LLM inference and scientific computing, yet Hopper 2:4 sparse GEMM remains poorly understood.
